articles.headline: Sammy Smith Extends Margin Atop Standings Without Visiting Victory Lane
articles.dek: Consistency keeps the eighth-tier regular at the head of the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series standings through six events.
articles.body:
Six races into the thirty-three race calendar, the top of the points table tells a straightforward story of accumulating solid finishes. Sammy Smith holds the premier position with 191 points, maintaining an advantage over Justin Allgaier despite having zero wins on the ledger compared to Allgaier's single triumph.

Darlington Raceway provided another textbook example of this methodical approach. Smith drove the eight machine from a sixth-place starting slot to a fourth-place finish, leading six laps along the way. That performance added another steady batch of points to an already healthy margin. Allgaier sits second with 184 points, seven markers back, backed by his win earlier in the year.

The battle directly behind the top two involves Parker Retzlaff in third with 167 points and Rajah Caruth holding fourth with 161 points. Caruth also remains winless, leaning on clean afternoon outings to maintain his standing inside the upper tier. Ryan Sieg rounds out the top five with 154 points.

With eighteen events left before the post-season eligibility cutoff after race twenty-four, the buffer Smith has built provides operational breathing room. While race winners secure direct entry safety, accumulating accumulated tallies week after week remains a viable path for drivers who consistently challenge inside the top ten without sweeping the checkered flags.
articles.author: Wes Ostrander

articles.headline: Austin Hill Dominates Darlington to Capture Second Win of Season
articles.dek: Austin Hill led 54 laps from the pole position to cruise to a victory in the Sport Clips Haircuts VFW Help A Hero 200.
articles.body:
Austin Hill proved untouchable on Saturday afternoon at Darlington Speedway, winning the Sport Clips Haircuts VFW Help A Hero 200 by a commanding margin of 7.638 seconds. Hill started from the pole in the 21 entry and controlled the 74-lap event, pacing the field for 54 laps on the unique egg-shaped oval under cloudy skies and 84-degree temperatures.

Corey Day crossed the finish line in second place after starting 15th and leading six laps. Rajah Caruth drove a steady race to claim third, while Sammy Smith finished fourth to maintain his grip on the top spot in the championship standings. Taylor Gray rounded out the top five in fifth position.

The race ran entirely without caution flags, allowing drivers to sort out their handling over long green-flag runs. William Sawalich charged through the pack from his 27th starting position to finish eighth, earning the biggest upward movement of the day. Justin Allgaier, who led eight laps, finished seventh.

Sammy Smith leads the championship standings with 191 points following the sixth event of the 33-race schedule. Justin Allgaier holds the second position with 184 points and one victory, while Parker Retzlaff sits third with 167 points and a win. Rajah Caruth moves to fourth with 161 points, and Ryan Sieg rounds out the top five at 154 points.

The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series continues next week as the sim field heads to the next stop on the calendar.

articles.headline: Parker Retzlaff Charges From Eighteenth to Win The LiUNA! at Las Vegas
articles.dek: Parker Retzlaff navigated a green-flag run through the desert heat to secure his first victory of the season at Las Vegas Motor Speedway.
articles.body:
Parker Retzlaff drove his number 99 machine from eighteenth on the starting grid to capture the victory in Saturday's The LiUNA! at Las Vegas Motor Speedway. Retzlaff led 31 laps of the 107-lap intermediate distance race, crossing the finish line 1.652 seconds ahead of the competition to become the third different winner in five events for the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series.

Sammy Smith finished second after starting fourth, maintaining his grip on the top spot in the championship standings. Ryan Sieg brought his machine home in third place. Rajah Caruth took fourth and Sheldon Creed rounded out the leading group in fifth after leading 31 laps earlier in the afternoon. The race ran under clear skies at 67 degrees and featured fourteen lead changes among ten different drivers. Only one caution slowed the pace during the 107 laps.

Pole sitter Corey Day saw his afternoon end early with header issues after leading the field to green, finishing thirty-sixth. Other retirements included Jeb Burton, Baltazar Leguizamón, Blaine Perkins, Kyle Sieg, and Jeremy Clements, while Dawson Cram and Austin Green exited due to accidents.

Sammy Smith leads the championship standings with 158 points following the Las Vegas round. Justin Allgaier holds second with 154 points and one victory. Parker Retzlaff jumps to third with 140 points and his newly minted win. Ryan Sieg sits fourth with 137 points and Anthony Alfredo rounds out the top five with 135 points.

The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series continues next week as the schedule moves to the next venue.

The early-season Chase battle in the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series has narrowed down to a single point at the cutline. Following the GOVX 200 at Phoenix Raceway, Taylor Gray holds the twelfth and final transfer spot with 89 points. Just behind him is Brandon Jones, sitting thirteenth with 87 points after four rounds of competition.

Jones put together a clean run in the desert, starting third and racing inside the top five all afternoon. The performance yielded a solid points haul, but it was not quite enough to clear the deficit to Gray.

- 12. Taylor Gray: 89 pts
- 13. Brandon Jones: 87 pts (-2)
- 14. Blaine Perkins: 80 pts (-9)

With twenty races remaining before the regular-season cutoff, the urgency for the mid-pack teams is rising. Jones has shown race pace, but consistency over the next stretch of intermediate tracks will dictate whether he can crack the top twelve.

articles.headline: Sheldon Creed Captures GOVX 200 Victory at Phoenix Raceway
articles.dek: Sheldon Creed held off Corey Day in the closing laps to win Saturday's NASCAR on JRN race at Phoenix Raceway.
articles.body:
Sheldon Creed drove to victory in the GOVX 200 at Phoenix Raceway on Saturday, navigating the final green flag run to beat Corey Day by 1.421 seconds. Creed started second in the 38-car field and led 24 laps of the 94-lap event, taking control late after pole-sitter Justin Allgaier dominated the first half of the race.

Allgaier led a race-high 53 laps from the pole in the NASCAR on JRN O'Reilly Auto Parts Series event. However, handling changes and a late cycle shuffled the #7 machine back, leaving Allgaier to finish ninth. Creed capitalized on the shifting conditions, managing his tires through the race's single caution period to secure his first win of the season.

Corey Day finished second after starting fifth and leading 17 laps, maintaining his strong early-season momentum. Brandon Jones finished third, followed by Anthony Alfredo in fourth. Austin Hill delivered the performance of the day, charging through the field from a 31st-place starting position to finish fifth.

Sammy Smith finished sixth, with Dean Thompson seventh and Taylor Gray eighth. Allgaier crossed the line ninth, and Rajah Caruth rounded out the top ten. Blaine Perkins was the race's lone retirement, dropping out due to a camshaft failure.

In the championship standings, Allgaier maintains the points lead with 126 points and one victory. Sammy Smith holds second with 123 points, three markers back. Corey Day sits third with 113 points and one win, while Anthony Alfredo climbs to fourth with 104 points.

The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series heads next to Atlanta Motor Speedway for Round 5 of the 33-race schedule.

articles.headline: Sawalich Nips Perkins at the Line to Win Daytona Opener
articles.dek: A last-lap charge off turn four gives William Sawalich the United Rentals 300 victory by 0.077 seconds.
articles.body:
DAYTONA BEACH, Fla. - William Sawalich edged Blaine Perkins by 0.077 seconds at Daytona International Speedway on Saturday, taking the season-opening United Rentals 300 in a dash to the line.

Sawalich started 25th and led only two laps in the No. 18, but timed his run off turn four on the 48th and final lap to drag-race Perkins to the checkered flag. Cleetus McFarland finished third, while Daniel Dye charged through the field from 32nd to take fourth. Brent Crews completed the top five.

"We bided our time near the back early and let everybody burn their stuff up," Sawalich said. "When the hole opened on the high side coming off turn four, I just stayed in the throttle. Getting one early takes a ton of pressure off this team."

The 48-lap race featured 15 lead changes among 12 drivers under clear, 51-degree skies. Pole sitter Jesse Love struggled to maintain track position in the draft, eventually sliding back to finish 21st.

Ryan Sieg and Parker Retzlaff did the heavy lifting out front through the afternoon. Sieg paced the field for a race-high 17 laps, while Retzlaff led 12 circuits. Both drivers found themselves shuffled backward during the final cycle of moves, with Retzlaff finishing seventh and Sieg crossing the stripe in eighth.

Perkins led two laps late and appeared positioned to hold off the outside lane entering the tri-oval, but Sawalich found clean air off the bumper of the trailing pack.

"Missed it by less than a tenth," Perkins said. "The 18 had a huge run off four and I tried to pinch him down, but he had too much momentum. Second hurts on a superspeedway, but it is solid points to open the year."

Two cautions slowed the event, keeping the 38-car grid bunched up. Several contenders hit trouble during the afternoon, with four drivers failing to make the finish. Ryan Ellis retired early due to an ignition failure, while Mason Maggio, Kyle Sieg, and Josh Williams pulled out of competition before the final restart.

The attrition and pack racing opened lanes for drivers starting deep in the order. In addition to Sawalich and Crews advancing from outside the top 20, Austin Green surged from 34th to finish sixth, Andrew Patterson went from 35th to ninth, and Sammy Smith rebounded from starting 38th to crack the top 10.

Dye made the biggest climb of the day, gaining 28 positions over 48 laps without pacing a single circuit.

"Starting thirty-second you just have to be smart and miss the mess," Dye said. "We picked them off three or four at a time on the restarts and the car had plenty of speed in clean air. P4 is a great start."

Sawalich leaves Daytona leading the standings with 40 points and an early win in the bank. Perkins ranks second with 35 points, followed by McFarland with 34, Dye with 33, and Crews with 32. Green (31), Retzlaff (30), Sieg (29), Patterson (28), and Smith (27) round out the top 10.

The series continues its 33-race schedule next week for round two.

interviews.quote: We kept our nose clean and brought home a good points day. That is what keeps you in the hunt all year long.
We had good speed in the middle stages of the run, but Austin just checked out on us. Second is solid for our team today.
That 21 machine was dialed in right from the drop of the green flag. We didn't give them a chance to catch us once we got out front.
Second place is solid points for our championship run, but we wanted to chase down the ninety-nine at the end.
We started deep in the pack and just had to stay patient while the car came to us on the long runs. The team gave me a fast piece.
Starting 31st makes for a long day, but our guys made good adjustments and the truck came alive in the second half.
Second hurts a little bit because we had the speed to win, but Sheldon ran a great race. We will take the points and go to Atlanta.
We had a fast truck right off the truck. Crew gave me a great setup and we just had to execute at the end.
We started deep in the pack and had to fight for every inch. Moving up nine spots on a road course with no cautions takes hard racing.
Second is decent for our day, but Allgaier had us covered at the end. We will take the points and go on to the next one.
Our car was hooked up all afternoon. We just had to bide our time, let the race come to us, and once we got out front we could stretch it.
We gave it everything we had on that final lap. Just came up a bumper short, but we will take the solid points day and move on.
Our car took everything we asked of it today. We had to wait for the right moment to make our move and it paid off at the line.
We started way back in thirty-second and just kept finding holes to slip through. Good points day for us.
Hate to lose it by that little, but a second-place finish at Daytona is a great start to the year for this team.
We just kept our nose clean and waited for the right lane to open up off turn four. Car was fast when we needed it.
Starting thirty-second you just have to be smart and miss the mess. We picked them off three or four at a time on the restarts and the car had plenty of speed in clean air. P4 is a great start.
Missed it by less than a tenth. The 18 had a huge run off four and I tried to pinch him down, but he had too much momentum. Second hurts on a superspeedway, but it is solid points to open the year.

We bided our time near the back early and let everybody burn their stuff up. When the hole opened on the high side coming off turn four, I just stayed in the throttle. Getting one early takes a ton of pressure off this team.
